Service

Crocodile Capture & Relocation

When other controls are impractical, we trap and relocate problem crocodiles — assessed case by case and fully permitted.

Sometimes a crocodile and a work site simply can’t share the same stretch of water. When spotting, exclusion and work-practice controls aren’t practical, our team removes the risk by capturing and relocating the animal — safely for your people and humanely for the crocodile.

What’s included

  • Site inspection and assessment of the animal, its behaviour and the risk it poses
  • Liaison on the permits and approvals required before any capture
  • Trap deployment, monitoring and checking to an agreed schedule
  • Hand, noose and trap capture by experienced operators
  • Safe restraint, transport and relocation or hand-over as directed by the relevant authority
  • A written job report for your records and HSE system

When you need it

A crocodile is regularly sighted where people work, fish, swim or launch boats

A crocodile is trapped or stranded in a pond, dam, drain or water-storage facility

Works must proceed in or beside water and the animal can’t be safely managed in place

Your risk assessment has ruled out lower-level controls

How it works

Do we need to capture? We work through these questions first.

  1. 1Can the work be planned away from the water?
    YES →Avoid: exclusion zones, timing, siting
  2. 2Must crews be near the water?
    YES →Watch: dedicated overwatch with stop-work authority
  3. 3Is the crew trained for crocodile country?
    YES →Train: toolbox talks and awareness training
  4. 4Is a specific crocodile still a risk the controls can’t manage?
    YES →Remove: permitted capture and relocation

If an earlier control manages the risk, we stop there — capture is the last resort.

From call-out to relocation

  1. 1Assess

    Inspect the site, the animal and its behaviour.

  2. 2Approve

    Confirm permits and directions with the relevant authority.

  3. 3Capture

    Trap, noose or hand capture by experienced operators.

  4. 4Secure

    Safe restraint for the animal and the team.

  5. 5Relocate

    Transport and relocation or hand-over as directed.

  6. 6Report

    Written job report for your records.

Questions

Is capture always the answer?

No. Capture is a last resort. We start with a risk assessment and recommend the least invasive control that keeps people safe — often overwatch, exclusion zones or changed work practices.

Do you need a permit to remove a crocodile?

Crocodiles are protected wildlife, so removal is controlled under state and territory law. We work within the approvals framework and help you arrange what’s required before any capture.

How long does a capture take?

It depends on the animal, the site and the method. Some captures happen in a single session; trapping can take days of monitoring. We’ll give you an honest plan after the site assessment.
